definitions.explanation: A large, important church that serves as the seat of a bishop, or more broadly, any grand and historically significant church building.

examples.japanese: パリの{大聖堂|だいせいどう}を{訪|おとず}れた。
examples.english: I visited the cathedral in Paris.

examples.japanese: ゴシック{様式|ようしき}の{大聖堂|だいせいどう}は{壮大|そうだい}だった。
この{大聖堂|だいせいどう}は{中世|ちゅうせい}に{建|た}てられ、{世界遺産|せかいいさん}に{登録|とうろく}されている。
examples.english: This cathedral was built in the Middle Ages and is registered as a World Heritage Site.

notes:
Composed of {大|だい} (great) + {聖堂|せいどう} (sacred hall/church). Refers specifically to large, historically significant churches, particularly European cathedrals.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ゴシック{大聖堂|だいせいどう}: Gothic cathedral
- {大聖堂|だいせいどう}を{訪|おとず}れる: to visit a cathedral
- {大聖堂|だいせいどう}の{内部|ないぶ}: the interior of a cathedral
- {大聖堂|だいせいどう}の{尖塔|せんとう}: a cathedral spire

RELATED WORDS:
- {聖堂|せいどう}: church, chapel — a smaller or more general sacred building
- {礼拝堂|れいはいどう}: chapel, prayer hall — a smaller place of worship
- {教会|きょうかい}: church — the most common general term for a Christian church

CULTURAL NOTE:
Japan has no medieval cathedrals of its own, so this word is primarily encountered when discussing European architecture, travel, history, and literature. Famous examples often referenced in Japanese media include ノートルダム{大聖堂|だいせいどう} (Notre-Dame Cathedral) and ケルン{大聖堂|だいせいどう} (Cologne Cathedral).
